sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: WNWLY MID LEVEL WINDS AT 50-70 KT ARE FORECAST TO EXTEND FROM THE PACIFIC NW INTO THE CENTRAL PLAINS AND EWD INTO THE MID ATLANTIC STATES THROUGH THE PERIOD. WEAK EMBEDDED SHORTWAVE TROUGHS WILL PROGRESS THROUGH THIS FLOW...THOUGH NONE OF THEM ARE FORECAST TO BE STRONG ENOUGH TO RESULT IN HEIGHT FALLS OR AMPLIFY THE ZONAL FLOW. AT THE SURFACE...A WEAK FRONT/REMNANT OUTFLOW BOUNDARY WILL LINGER EAST OF THE APPALACHIANS SEWD INTO GULF COASTAL STATES. ANOTHER WEAK COLD FRONT/TROUGH IS FORECAST TO EXTEND FROM THE WRN GREAT LAKES SEWD INTO THE CENTRAL PLAINS BY LATE AFTERNOON.

sections.title: NRN/CENTRAL MO EWD INTO THE LOWER OH/TN VALLEYS
sections.text: SHORTWAVE TROUGH...WHICH WAS MOVING THROUGH WY WED EVENING...IS FORECAST TO MOVE INTO NRN MO THU AFTERNOON AND INTO IL DURING THE EVENING. LARGE SCALE LIFTING ASSOCIATED WITH THIS SYSTEM... COMBINED WITH EFFECTIVE SHEAR AT 40-50 KT AND MLCAPES FROM 1000 TO 2000 J/KG...FAVOR ORGANIZED SEVERE CONVECTION DEVELOPING EWD THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING FROM MO INTO THE WRN OH VALLEY. VEERING WINDS AND STRONG 1 KM SHEAR MAY SUPPORT A TORNADO THREAT...ESPECIALLY ACROSS PORTIONS OF MO...WHERE SURFACE DEWPOINTS SHOULD BE AT LEAST IN THE MID 60S AND STRONG LOW LEVEL SHEAR WILL EXIST. HOWEVER... THE PRIMARY SEVERE THREAT IS MORE LIKELY TO BE WIND DAMAGE...GIVEN THE STRONGER FLOW ALOFT AND MOSTLY UNIDIRECTIONAL WLY FLOW ALOFT.

sections.title: SERN KS/SWRN MO/NRN AND CENTRAL OK/NWRN AR
sections.text: MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER...DEWPOINTS AOA 70F...AND AFTERNOON HEATING WILL LEAD TO A VERY UNSTABLE AIRMASS...MLCAPES IN EXCESS OF 3000 J/KG. HOWEVER...LACK OF ANY EVIDENT DYNAMICAL FORCING AND STRONG CAPPING BETWEEN 800 AND 700 MB WILL LIKELY INHIBIT STORM DEVELOPMENT THROUGH THE DAYLIGHT HOURS. SHOULD ANY STORMS FORM... DEEP LAYER SHEAR AND INSTABILITY WOULD BE SUPPORTIVE OF SUPERCELLS WITH VERY LARGE HAIL. HOWEVER...THUNDERSTORMS ARE MORE LIKELY OVERNIGHT AS BOUNDARY SAGS SLOWLY SEWD INTO FAR SERN KS/SWRN MO/NRN OK AND LOW LEVEL JET/WARM ADVECTION INTENSIFIES. GIVEN THE DEGREE OF INSTABILITY...30-40 KT MID LEVEL WNWLY FLOW AND SURFACE BOUNDARY...AN MCS WITH HAIL AND BOWING SEGMENTS/WIND APPEARS LIKELY...MAINLY AFTER 05Z.

sections.title: MID ATLANTIC STATES SEWD INTO THE GULF COASTAL STATES
sections.text: MODERATE INSTABILITY WILL OCCUR IN AREAS WHERE MOIST AIR MASS IS WARMED FROM MORNING/EARLY AFTERNOON SUNSHINE. STORMS SHOULD READILY DEVELOP DURING THE AFTERNOON ALONG A WEAK BOUNDARY LOCATED IN THE REGION. MID LEVEL WLY WINDS AT 25 TO 40 KT WILL BE FAVORABLE FOR MULTICELL SEVERE STORM CLUSTERS. LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS SHOULD BE THE PRIMARY SEVERE THREATS...DUE TO THE DEGREE OF INSTABILITY AND MOSTLY UNDIRECTIONAL WLY FLOW ABOVE THE BOUNDARY LAYER. STRONGER STORMS WILL BE DIURNALLY MODULATED... WITH ACTIVITY EXPECTED TO DIMINISH AROUND SUNSET. ..IMY/JEWELL.. 05/07/2009

sections.title: CENTRAL/SRN PLAINS INTO THE MID MS/OH RIVER VALLEYS
sections.text: BROAD MID/UPPER LEVEL TROUGH ACROSS THE NRN TIER OF THE CONUS WILL MAINTAIN SEASONABLY STRONG WLY FLOW ALOFT ACROSS MUCH OF THE CENTRAL STATES THROUGH THE PERIOD. A SERIES OF LOW AMPLITUDE SHORTWAVE TROUGHS EVIDENT THIS MORNING ON WV IMAGERY WILL MOVE QUICKLY THROUGH THIS ZONAL FLOW REGIME AND SHOULD SERVE TO FOCUS MORE CONCENTRATED AREAS OF STRONG/SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS TODAY. LEADING IMPULSE MOVING RAPIDLY OVER THE MID MO RIVER VALLEY EARLY THIS MORNING WILL CONTINUE EWD ACROSS THE MIDWEST. THIS SHOULD PROVIDE IMPETUS FOR THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT FROM THE MID MS RIVER VALLEY EWD ACROSS THE SRN GREAT LAKES/OH RIVER VALLEYS TODAY AS AIR MASS BECOMES MARGINALLY TO MODERATELY UNSTABLE. REGION WILL REMAIN REMOVED FROM RICHER GULF MOISTURE TRAPPED BEHIND SURFACE FRONT PERSISTING ACROSS THE CENTRAL GULF COAST STATES. HOWEVER...FORECAST SOUNDINGS INDICATE AREA OF 500-1300 J/KG MLCAPE AHEAD OF THIS FEATURE WITH SHEAR SUPPORTIVE OF ORGANIZED LINES AND SUPERCELLS. LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE PRIMARY THREATS...ALTHOUGH AN ISOLATED TORNADO CAN ALSO BE EXPECTED ESPECIALLY WITH WWD EXTENT INTO MID 60F SURFACE DEWPOINTS INTO MO. FARTHER WEST...SURFACE LOW WILL PERSIST OVER THE HIGH PLAIN

sections.title: SRN MID ATLANTIC/CAROLINAS INTO CENTRAL GULF COAST STATES
sections.text: PRONOUNCED VORT MAX AND ASSOCIATED SHORTWAVE TROUGH IS MOVING ACROSS WRN VA/NC EARLY THIS MORNING. EXTENSIVE THUNDERSTORMS/MOIST CONVECTION ALREADY ONGOING AHEAD OF THIS FEATURE SHOULD LIMIT OVERALL DESTABILIZATION EARLY TODAY. HOWEVER...12Z SOUNDINGS INDICATE MODEST MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND DEEP LAYER SHEAR OVER THE REGION. THEREFORE...SEVERE THREAT MAY INCREASE THROUGH THE MORNING...WITH DEVELOPMENT OF STRONG/SEVERE STORMS LATER TODAY IN WAKE OF THIS ACTIVITY MORE CONDITIONAL. DEEP LAYER SHEAR WANES WITH SWWD EXTENT ALONG STALLED SURFACE FRONT INTO THE CENTRAL GULF COAST STATES. HOWEVER...STRONG INSTABILITY AND 20-30 KT EFFECTIVE SHEAR SHOULD PROVE MORE THAN ADEQUATE FOR CLUSTERS/LINES OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS NEAR THIS FRONT THROUGH THE DAY PRODUCING ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. SUBSTANTIAL MID LEVEL DRYING THIS MORNING ON AREA SOUNDINGS AND WV IMAGERY MAY FAVOR CORRIDOORS OF WIND DAMAGE WITH THE MORE INTENSE CLUSTERS INTO THE EARLY EVENING. ..EVANS/GARNER.. 05/07/2009

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: FAST WESTERLIES BY THE END OF THE FORECAST PERIOD WILL STRETCH FROM OREGON TO PA AROUND 42N. ONCE TROUGH NOW MID ATLANTIC STATES MOVES OFFSHORE ADDITIONAL IMPULSES EMBEDDED WITHIN THE POLAR JET STREAM ARE OF LITTLE AMPLITUDE AND DIFFICULT TO FOLLOW. RICH GULF AIR MASS SRN STATES WILL BE RETURNING NWD THRU CENTRAL PLAINS AND MID MS VALLEY THRU TONIGHT AS PRESSURES FALL HIGH PLAINS IN RESPONSE TO DEVELOPMENT OF LEE LOW. EML CONTINUES TO SPREAD EWD ACROSS SRN PLAINS INTO LOWER MS VALLEY EFFECTIVELY CAPPING OFF MUCH OF THE CONVECTIVE POTENTIAL THAT AREA. HOWEVER A PRONOUNCED MID LVL THERMAL RIBBON SETS UP JUST S OF THE UPPER JET AND BECOMES AN EFFECTIVE SOURCE OF WARM ADVECTION LATER TONIGHT AS LOW LEVEL JET INCREASES SRN INTO CENTRAL PLAINS.

sections.title: MID ATLANTIC COAST SWWD TO GULF STATES
sections.text: WHILE PRIMARY MID LEVEL TROUGH CURRENTLY MOVING OFFSHORE ALONG WITH ORGANIZED CONVECTION...THE AIR MASS REMAINS MOIST AND POTENTIALLY MDTLY UNSTABLE E OF CENTRAL APPALACHIANS TO THE GULF COAST STATES. STRONG HEATING WILL PUSH MLCAPES TO AOA 1500 J/KG THIS AREA AS WELL AS DISSIPATING MUCH OF THE CINH BY MID AFTERNOON. SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS WILL BE COMMON WITH THE GENERALLY MARGINAL SHEAR...PARTICULARLY IN LOWER LEVELS... FAVORING PRIMARILY A MULTI-CELL MODE. LARGE HAIL AND LOCAL DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE ASSOCIATED WITH STRONGEST STORMS...WITH THE THREAT DECREASING SOON AFTER SUNSET. NOSE OF THE POLAR JET CROSSES CENTRAL APPALACHIANS BY THIS EVENING PROVIDING ENHANCED UPPER LEVEL DIVERGENCE WHICH COULD SUPPORT THE MORE ORGANIZED THUNDERSTORMS THE 12Z NAM GENERATES ERN NC/SERN VA THIS EVENING.

sections.title: CENTRAL PLAINS/LOWER MO/OH VALLEYS
sections.text: LOW LEVEL MOISTURE RAPIDLY RETURNING ACROSS OK/KS UNDER THE STRONG CAP. BY LATER THIS AFTERNOON 60F DEWPOINTS WILL SPREAD NEWD AHEAD OF WEAK SURFACE FRONT EXTENDING FROM IA INTO SWRN KS. THE CAP WILL BE CONSIDERABLY WEAKER ACROSS NERN KS INTO NRN MO AND WITH HEATING CINH WILL HAVE SUFFICIENTLY DISSIPATED TO ALLOW THUNDERSTORMS TO DEVELOP ALONG AND JUST AHEAD OF THE WEAK FRONTAL ZONE. WITH MLCAPES OF 2000 J/KG ALONG WITH STEEP MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES IN EXCESS OF 8C/KM THE AIR MASS WILL BE PRIMED FOR SEVERE STORMS BY MID/LATE AFTERNOON. WHILE ANY EMBEDDED IMPULSES IN THE FAST FLOW HARD TO IDENTIFY...COMBINATION OF 50-60 KT OF SHEAR AND FAVORABLE THERMODYNAMICS...SUPERCELLS EXPECTED TO BE THE INITIAL MODE. DURING THE EVENING STORMS WOULD LIKELY EVOLVE MORE INTO LINE SEGMENTS/BOWS AS THEY MOVE S OF E ACROSS LOWER MO VALLEY. VERY LARGE HAIL AND ISOLATED TORNADO THREAT WOULD BE INITIAL THREAT WITH ANY SUPERCELL TRANSITIONING INTO MORE OF A WIND DAMAGE CONCERN AS STORMS EVOLVE INTO MORE OF A LINEAR MODE. OVERNIGHT STRONG WARM ADVECTION SETS ACROSS KS INTO NRN OK AS LOW LEVEL JET INCREASES TO 50KTS AND E/W SURFACE BOUNDARY SETTLES SWD THRU KS. WITH THE RICH GULF AIR NOW SRN PLAINS STREAMING

sections.title: SERN NEB/KS/NRN OK EWD TO THE MID MS VALLEY
sections.text: STORMS CONTINUE TO DEVELOP OVER SERN NEB AND ADJACENT SWRN IA...NEAR A WEAK SURFACE LOW WHERE THE AIRMASS HAS BECOME MARGINALLY-UNSTABLE WITH AFTERNOON HEATING. FAVORABLY VEERING/SHEARED FLOW WITH HEIGHT WILL SUPPORT SUPERCELLS...WITH ASSOCIATED THREATS FOR HAIL/LOCALLY-DAMAGING WINDS AND PERHAPS A COUPLE OF TORNADOES. ADDITIONAL CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED SWD INTO ERN KS...WITH STORMS SPREADING ESEWD WITH TIME ALONG WITH ACCOMPANYING SEVERE POTENTIAL. FARTHER S...A CAPPED BOUNDARY LAYER SHOULD INHIBIT ALL BUT AN ISOLATED STORM OR TWO ACROSS OK THIS AFTERNOON..BUT AN INTENSIFYING LOW-LEVEL JET ACROSS THE SRN PLAINS WILL SUPPORT MORE WIDESPREAD STORM DEVELOPMENT THIS EVENING/OVERNIGHT. IT APPEARS THAT A GENERALLY WNW-ESE BAND OF STRONG/SEVERE CONVECTION WILL DEVELOP ACROSS PARTS OF KS/OK -- NEAR AND S OF THE AFOREMENTIONED ONGOING STORMS. STORMS MAY DEVELOP AS FAR W AS SWRN KS...WITH AN MCS LIKELY TO EVOLVE WITH TIME AND THEN SPREAD ESEWD ACROSS SRN MO/NRN AR. THREAT FOR HAIL -- AND POSSIBLY LOCALLY-DAMAGING WINDS -- WILL ACCOMPANY THESE STORMS...WHICH MAY SPREAD AS FAR E AS THE TN VALLEY REGION LATE. GIVEN DEGREE OF INSTABILITY AND SHEAR SUPPORTIVE OF SUPERCELLS...VERY LARG

sections.title: VA/CAROLINAS/SRN GA AND VICINITY
sections.text: SCATTERED STORMS ONGOING ATTM ACROSS ERN KY/ERN TN/SRN WV AND INTO VA/NC/SC SHOULD CONTINUE TO INCREASE/SPREAD EWD WITH TIME...AHEAD OF A SHORT-WAVE TROUGH CROSSING THE LOWER OH/TN VALLEY REGION ATTM. MODERATE INSTABILITY /GENERALLY 1000 TO 1500 J/KG MIXED-LAYER CAPE/ WHICH HAS DEVELOPED ACROSS THE REGION COMBINED WITH INCREASING MID-LEVEL FLOW THROUGH THE AFTERNOON WILL SUPPORT A CONTINUED THREAT FOR ISOLATED STRONGER/ORGANIZED STORMS...AND ASSOCIATED THREATS FOR HAIL AND/OR LOCALLY-DAMAGING WINDS AND POSSIBLY AN ISOLATED TORNADO. WHILE DECREASING INSTABILITY SHOULD RESULT IN A SLOW DECREASE IN CONVECTIVE COVERAGE/INTENSITY THIS EVENING...A FEW STRONGER CELLS MAY PERSIST INTO THE LATE EVENING HOURS AS THE UPPER FEATURE CROSSES THIS AREA. ..GOSS.. 05/07/2009 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1120 AM CDT THU MAY 07 2009/

sections.title: SOUTH CENTRAL PLAINS INTO PARTS OF THE OZARK PLATEAU
sections.text: A LOW AMPLITUDE MID-LEVEL WAVE MAY BE IN THE PROCESS OF MIGRATING EASTWARD ACROSS THE CENTRAL ROCKIES. BUT...A MUCH MORE PROMINENT IMPULSE IS ALSO DIGGING ACROSS THE NORTHERN INTERMOUNTAIN REGION...AND PROGGED TO CONTINUE INTO THE NORTH CENTRAL ROCKIES OVERNIGHT. AS THIS OCCURS...LOWER/MID TROPOSPHERIC WARM ADVECTION APPEARS LIKELY TO STRENGTHEN THIS EVENING ACROSS THE CENTRAL PLAINS...ON THE NOSE OF AN INTENSIFYING LOW-LEVEL JET...ON THE EDGE OF STRONGER CAPPING ELEVATED MIXED LAYER AIR. THIS IS EXPECTED TO BE ACCOMPANIED BY INCREASING CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT ...PERHAPS FIRST ACROSS PARTS OF NORTHWEST OKLAHOMA/SOUTHWESTERN KANSAS. THIS MAY NOT OCCUR UNTIL NEAR OR SHORTLY AFTER 06Z...BUT IN THE PRESENCE OF STRONG INSTABILITY ASSOCIATED WITH HIGH LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE CONTENT /CHARACTERIZED BY SURFACE DEW POINTS NEAR 70F/ AND STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES...STORMS PROBABLY WILL QUICKLY BECOME SEVERE. DEEP LAYER SHEAR ON THE SOUTHERN FRINGE OF 30-50 KT WESTERLY FLOW WILL BE SUFFICIENT FOR SUPERCELLS. MODELS SUGGEST THAT THE LOW-LEVEL JET WILL STRENGTHEN IN EXCESS OF 50 KTS OVERNIGHT...GRADUALLY VEERING FROM SOUTHERLY TO WEST SOUTHWESTERLY. THIS...COUPLED WITH FAVORABLE LARGE-SCALE FORCING.

sections.title: MIDDLE MISSISSIPPI/LOWER OHIO VALLEY
sections.text: BETTER LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE APPEARS LIKELY TO REMAIN GENERALLY CUT OFF FROM THE REGION THROUGH THIS PERIOD. BUT...LINGERING INSTABILITY MAY REMAIN SUFFICIENT TO SUPPORT A CONTINUING SEVERE RISK WITH ONGOING STORMS WHICH HAVE FORMED ALONG A BAROCLINIC ZONE EXTENDING ACROSS NORTHERN MISSOURI/CENTRAL ILLINOIS INTO THE LOWER OHIO VALLEY. ACTIVITY IS BEING SUPPORTED BY FORCING ASSOCIATED WITH A DIGGING LOW AMPLITUDE MID-LEVEL IMPULSE...WHICH IS PROGGED TO GRADUALLY TURN EASTWARD INTO THE LOWER OHIO VALLEY OVERNIGHT.

sections.title: MID ATLANTIC STATES
sections.text: CONVECTIVE POTENTIAL FOR THE MOST PART APPEARS TO BE DIMINISHING. HOWEVER...FORCING ASSOCIATED WITH A LOW AMPLITUDE WAVE TURNING EAST OF THE CENTRAL APPALACHIANS COULD STILL CONTRIBUTE TO VIGOROUS STORM DEVELOPMENT THIS EVENING...PARTICULARLY ACROSS PARTS OF NORTHEASTERN NORTH CAROLINA THROUGH 03-06Z. ..KERR.. 05/08/2009
